episodes.synopsis: Hiroko is damn good at her job, but the stress is eating her alive. An interview with a politician may lead to her biggest scoop yet, but there’s a cost to everything.
episodes.title: The Female Hataraki Man

episodes.synopsis: Fumiya really doesn’t like his job and likes Hiroko even less. But the job comes first, and he needs help on a stakeout…
episodes.title: Stakeout Man

episodes.synopsis: Pointless meetings prevent employees from actually doing their work. Hiroko is NOT happy when her pitch for an article is reassigned to someone else.
episodes.title: Ramen Man

episodes.synopsis: Someone needs to make sure important things get done. However, is it worth it when it puts a strain on a relationship?
episodes.title: Apology Man

episodes.synopsis: Mayu discovers that she’s been sidelined in favor of Hiroko as a serial lead due to lack of experience.
episodes.title: Double Back Man

episodes.synopsis: An employee must navigate the murky waters of office politics and gossip carefully. Getting involved, no matter how well-intentioned, can have repercussions.
episodes.title: Princess Man

episodes.synopsis: Everyone needs a break to avoid burnout. Hiroko is a regular client of Midoriko, a massage therapist. Do both women have something to teach the other?
episodes.title: Meticulous Man

episodes.synopsis: Makoto Chiba works in sales. It’s an important job, but it can also be thankless. But that’s ok, it’s enough if a book sells well. At least, that’s what he tells himself.
episodes.title: Reward Man

episodes.synopsis: Hiroko had an interview lined up, but the man died of heart failure from overworking. Whether she wishes to or not, Hiroko finds herself affected by this.
episodes.title: Accomplished Hataraki Man

episodes.synopsis: Personal problems can bleed over into work. In comparison to Hiroko’s life, Maiko seems to have everything figured out.
episodes.title: Incapable Hataraki Man

episodes.synopsis: Hiroko and Shinji both consistently choose their careers over their relationship, which is now at a breaking point. Can things really continue as they are now?
episodes.title: Nevertheless, Hataraki Man
